integrity.deterministic_path: The graph proposes edges via degree-normalized L3. Claude reads, adjudicates, explains. Claude never invents an edge.
integrity.no_citation_no_render: Every mechanistic clause opens to a real PubMed paper.
integrity.predicted_labeled: Predicted structures are always labelled predicted with a confidence number (pLDDT/ipTM). Never shown as experimental fact.
integrity.locked_evaluator: The held-out split was frozen and committed BEFORE any prediction code, in a module the reasoning layer cannot import.
integrity.headline_is_honest: Precision is computed on real held-out Gordon edges, not the prototype's illustrative 80%.

eval.protocol: seeded random 17% sample of the 332 HC Gordon viral->host edges, plus disclosed pinned walkthrough edge(s). Precision reported with and without pinned edges.

loop.measured_on: the remaining held-out edges (fair before/after, same target set)
loop.story: Confirm the high-confidence recovered-true edges (each L3-rank #1, each a real Gordon edge), fold them back as known, and re-score the still-hidden edges on the same target set. Folding them back re-ranks the still-hidden edges — one climbs into the top 20 — lifting precision@20 from 0.3 to 0.35. Reachability is unchanged this round; the gain is honest re-ranking, not newly-unlocked edges.

flagship.note: Recovered via a genuine length-3 path (Orf6->NUP98->NUP214->RAE1). Topology ranks it inside Orf6's nuclear-pore candidate set; the structure (PDB 7VPH) and literature identify it as the biologically correct edge.

mechanism.text: SARS-CoV-2 ORF6 docks its short acidic C-terminal tail onto the RAE1–NUP98 mRNA-export complex at the cytoplasmic face of the nuclear pore
, inserting Met58 into the RAE1 mRNA-binding groove to sterically block bidirectional nucleocytoplasmic transport
, which prevents nuclear import of activated STAT1/STAT2 and antagonizes the type-I interferon response
. The graph proposed this edge from topology alone (Orf6→NUP98→NUP214→RAE1); the experimental structure shown above (PDB 7VPH, openable) resolves ORF6 in direct contact with RAE1.

citations.title: SARS-CoV-2 Orf6 hijacks Nup98 to block STAT nuclear import and antagonize interferon signaling.
citations.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
citations.claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf6 binds the Nup98–Rae1 complex at the nuclear pore to block STAT1/STAT2 nuclear import, antagonizing interferon signaling (Miorin et al. 2020 PNAS).

citations.title: Structural basis for Sarbecovirus ORF6 mediated blockage of nucleocytoplasmic transport.
citations.claim: Crystal structure of the SARS-CoV-2 Orf6 C-terminus bound to Rae1–Nup98 shows Orf6 inserts a methionine into the Rae1 mRNA-binding groove to sterically block nucleocytoplasmic transport.

citations.title: SARS-CoV-2 ORF6 Disrupts Bidirectional Nucleocytoplasmic Transport through Interactions with Rae1 and Nup98.
citations.claim: Orf6 docks onto the Rae1–Nup98 nucleoporin complex and disrupts bidirectional nucleocytoplasmic transport, inhibiting both host mRNA export and protein import.

structure.chains: SARS-CoV-2 ORF6 C-terminal tail + human RAE1 + human NUP98
structure.interface_source: computed: ORF6 heavy-atom contacts with RAE1 <= 3.0 Å in PDB 7VPH
structure.note: Experimental structure. ORF6 directly contacts RAE1 at the mRNA-export groove; the graph independently re-proposed this held-out edge and the structure confirms it.

proposed_test.text: Mutate the structure-verified ORF6 interface residues (E55A / M58R / D61A) and test for loss of RAE1 binding by co-immunoprecipitation in HEK293T; rescue of STAT1 nuclear import confirms the edge is functional.

druggability.curated_note: Shallow mRNA-export groove — addressable only as a PPI-inhibitor class.

mechanism.text: SARS-CoV-2 ORF9b occupies the TOM70 cytosolic C-terminal pocket that normally receives HSP90-chaperoned client proteins
, binding the chaperone-docking groove (structure-verified contacts include S53, R58, E65) and preventing the TOM70–HSP90 interaction
, which dampens TOM70-dependent MAVS signalling to blunt type-I interferon induction
. S53 is the phospho-regulated serine that tunes this interface.

citations.title: Crystal structure of SARS-CoV-2 Orf9b in complex with human TOM70 suggests unusual virus-host interactions.
citations.claim: Crystal structure of SARS-CoV-2 Orf9b bound to human TOM70 shows Orf9b occupies the TOM70 cytosolic C-terminal HSP70/HSP90-binding pocket, suggesting displacement of chaperone-mediated preprotein import.

citations.title: Binding of SARS-CoV-2 protein ORF9b to mitochondrial translocase TOM70 prevents its interaction with chaperone HSP90.
citations.claim: Biophysical characterization confirms SARS-CoV-2 Orf9b binds the mitochondrial translocase receptor TOM70, occupying its chaperone-docking groove.

citations.title: SARS-CoV-2 Orf9b suppresses type I interferon responses by targeting TOM70.
citations.claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf9b suppresses type I interferon responses by targeting TOM70, blocking the TOM70–MAVS mitochondrial antiviral signaling axis.

citations.title: Phosphorylation of SARS-CoV-2 Orf9b Regulates Its Targeting to Two Binding Sites in TOM70 and Recruitment of Hsp90.
citations.claim: Phosphorylation of SARS-CoV-2 Orf9b regulates its targeting to two binding sites in TOM70 and its recruitment of Hsp90, tuning the Orf9b–TOM70 chaperone interface.

structure.interface_source: computed: ORF9b heavy-atom contacts with TOM70 <= 3.0 Å in PDB 7DHG
structure.note: Experimental. S53 (the phospho-regulated serine) confirmed as a real contact; the prototype's S55/K46 are NOT contacts and were repaired.

proposed_test.text: Point-mutate the ORF9b interface (S53A phospho-null; R58E charge reversal) and confirm loss of TOM70 binding by co-immunoprecipitation; rescue of the MAVS-driven IFN-β reporter confirms functional relief.

druggability.curated_note: Defined hydrophobic TPR pocket — a more tractable orthosteric handle than most PPI interfaces.

mechanism.text: The SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein binds G3BP1 through a convergently-evolved ITFG/ΦxFG-like G3BP1-binding motif
, phase-separating with the G3BP scaffold to disassemble host stress granules and free the antiviral G3BP1 pool
, which suppresses the stress-granule-associated interferon response and favours viral replication
. Known AP-MS edge; the complex is not crystallised, so the 3D panel shows the predicted G3BP1 model, labelled predicted.

citations.title: Convergent evolution of the G3BP1-binding motif in betacoronavirus nucleocapsid proteins.
citations.claim: Betacoronavirus nucleocapsid proteins convergently evolved an ITFG (ΦxFG-like) G3BP1-binding motif that mediates the N–G3BP1 interaction and stress-granule antagonism.

citations.title: SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein phase separates with G3BPs to disassemble stress granules and facilitate viral production.
citations.claim: SARS-CoV-2 N protein phase-separates with G3BP1/G3BP2, disassembling host stress granules by co-condensing the G3BP scaffold away from stress-granule seeds.

citations.title: SARS-CoV-2 N Protein Antagonizes Stress Granule Assembly and IFN Production by Interacting with G3BPs to Facilitate Viral Replication.
citations.claim: SARS-CoV-2 N protein antagonizes stress-granule assembly through its interaction with G3BP1, suppressing the stress-granule-associated interferon response.

structure.chains: human G3BP1 (predicted monomer; the N–G3BP1 complex is not deposited)
structure.interface_source: no deposited complex; specific N-protein contact residues are not shown (would be unverified). Binding is via the literature-verified ITFG/ΦxFG G3BP1-binding motif.
structure.note: PREDICTED structure of the human G3BP1 target, shown to demonstrate the predicted-vs-experimental integrity path. Not the complex; not experimental fact.

proposed_test.text: Mutate the N-protein ITFG G3BP1-binding motif and test for loss of G3BP1 binding by co-immunoprecipitation; score rescue of stress-granule assembly by immunofluorescence. (Specific residue numbers await a complex structure.)

druggability.curated_note: NTF2-like groove; shallow PPI-inhibitor target, no known chemical starts.

skeptic.caveat: AP-MS captures co-complex membership, not necessarily a direct binary contact; treat as a co-membership prior until a structure resolves it.

mechanism.text: SARS-CoV-2 ORF6 binds the nucleoporin NUP98 as part of the Rae1–Nup98 export module at the nuclear pore
, and overexpression dislocates RAE1 and NUP98 from the pore, disrupting its integrity
. This is a known high-confidence AP-MS edge, shown for calibration.
